mainTopic: When a fetus counts as born (head versus most of the body), and relying on רוב for an unknown miscarriage
overview: The amud opens with the closing line of a discussion about ערכין. It then turns to a fetus that comes out in pieces or feet-first. רבי אלעזר says the head does not count as birth here until most of the body is out, while רבי יוחנן says the head alone counts. The גמרא asks whether this depends on שמואל's rule about נפלים, gives other versions of the dispute, and defends רבי יוחנן from the wording of the משנה. רב פפא and רב זביד link the dispute to a ברייתא, and the ברייתא defines 'most of the head' in three ways. A new משנה then covers a miscarriage of unknown kind. The גמרא tests רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule that we follow the majority of women, who give birth to a real baby, both against the משנה and against a ברייתא about an animal's בכור. The amud ends as רבין reports an objection from the law of a טועה, which is explained on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing line: the verse is needed to separate a man's valuation from a woman's
steps.stepSummary: The earlier discussion ends here. The verse about ערכין is needed to give a man and a woman different valuations, so it cannot also be used for another lesson.
steps.simpleTranslation: …to make a distinction between the valuation of a man and the valuation of a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the previous discussion about ערכין. The גמרא is finishing its answer: that verse is already 'busy' teaching that men and women have different valuations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion asked why a verse could not teach that a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס are left out of ערכין. The answer ends here: the verse is used to set a different value for a man and for a woman. So the lesson about the טומטום and אנדרוגינוס must come from other extra words in the verse.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed valuation from the תורה that someone pledges to the בית המקדש, based on a person's age and gender
The topic of valuation pledges
To make a distinction between

phrases.english: To distinguish between the valuation of a man
and the valuation of a woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְחַלֵּק בֵּין עֵרֶךְ אִישׁ לְעֵרֶךְ אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from the previous discussion, which began before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the verse is already used for a different lesson
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse about ערכין is needed to give men and women different valuations.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: even if the head came out, it is not yet a birth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a fetus that came out in pieces or feet-first. רבי אלעזר says the rule of 'most of the body' applies even if the head is among the parts that came out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if it came out in pieces or feet-first, etc. רבי אלעזר said: this applies even if the head is among the parts that came out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. רבי אלעזר explains that line: until most of the body is out, it is not a birth, even if the head is already out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a fetus that comes out in pieces or feet-first counts as born once most of it is out. רבי אלעזר says the head gets no special status here. If the head came out but most of the body did not, it still does not count as a birth.

keyTerms.meaning: Cut up, coming out in pieces
Reversed, coming out feet-first instead of head-first
Etc., the rest of the line in the משנה
The head is among them (among the parts that came out)

steps.confusionAlert: Usually, when a baby comes out head-first, the head coming out counts as birth. רבי אלעזר is talking only about the unusual cases in this משנה: a fetus in pieces or feet-first.

phrases.english: If it came out in pieces or reversed, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: once most of its body is out, it counts as born.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Even if the head is among them.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָצָא מְחוּתָּךְ אוֹ מְסוֹרָס וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a fetus in pieces or feet-first, only most of the body counts as birth, even if the head already came out.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: if the head came out, the head counts as birth
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן limits the משנה to a case where the head did not come out. If the head did come out, the head alone counts as birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: the משנה only taught its rule for a case where the head was not among the parts that came out. But if the head was among them, the head counts as birth (הראש פוטר).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees with רבי אלעזר. He says the משנה's 'most of the body' rule applies only when the head has not come out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the head is enough on its own. Once it is out, the fetus counts as born, even in pieces or feet-first. 'The head exempts' means the head coming out counts as a birth, with all its results. One example: the next child born is not a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this for…; a phrase that limits the case of a משנה
Exempts; here, the head counts as birth, so it 'opens the womb'
The status of a firstborn

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main argument of the section: does the head alone count as birth, or only most of the body? The rest of the discussion is built on it.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין הָרֹאשׁ עִמָּהֶן,
phrases.english: They taught this only where the head is not among them,
but if the head is among them —
the head exempts.
phrases.notes: He means the head coming out already counts as the birth. So whoever comes out after it is not a בכור.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין הָרֹאשׁ עִמָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second view that disagrees with רבי אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the head comes out, it counts as birth, even for a fetus in pieces or feet-first.

steps.title: Do they argue about שמואל's rule for non-viable fetuses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests their argument may depend on שמואל's rule that the head does not count as birth for נפלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say they argue about שמואל's opinion? שמואל said: the head does not count as birth for נפלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the argument between רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן is really about שמואל's rule. This sets up the next part of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל holds that for a נפל (a fetus that cannot survive), the head coming out does not count as birth. The suggestion is that רבי אלעזר agrees with שמואל, since a fetus in pieces is like a נפל. On this reading, רבי יוחנן disagrees and says the head counts as birth even for a נפל.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say?; the גמרא suggests an idea that it may later reject
They argue about
Non-viable fetuses that cannot survive

steps.confusionAlert: A 'לימא' question is often turned down later in the discussion. Don't treat this suggestion as the final answer.

phrases.english: Shall we say they argue about the view of Shmuel?
For Shmuel said:
The head does not exempt in the case of non-viable fetuses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to explain the argument in steps 2 and 3 by linking it to שמואל's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the argument between רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן the same as the question of whether the head counts as birth for נפלים?

steps.title: Everyone agrees about a whole fetus; they argue only about one born in pieces
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the dispute depends on שמואל. Both agree that the head counts as birth for a whole נפל. They argue only about a fetus that came out in pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a whole fetus, nobody argues. They argue about one that came out in pieces. One holds that the head counts only for a whole fetus, not for one in pieces. The other holds that the head counts for one in pieces too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from Step 4. It says the argument is not about שמואל at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4, the גמרא suggested that רבי אלעזר follows שמואל and רבי יוחנן does not. Now it says both agree the head counts for a whole נפל, which goes against שמואל. The real argument is narrower: does the head still count when the fetus comes out in pieces? רבי אלעזר says no, and רבי יוחנן says yes.

keyTerms.meaning: Whole: a fetus that came out in one piece
Cut up: a fetus that came out in pieces
Everyone agrees, and there is no argument
One master holds: a way of laying out each side of a dispute

phrases.english: With a whole fetus, everyone agrees,
when they disagree, it is about one in pieces,
for one master holds: it is only with a whole one that the head counts,
phrases.notes: This first master is רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: but with one in pieces, it does not count,
and the other master holds: with one in pieces, it also counts.
phrases.notes: This second master is רבי יוחנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: בשלם דכולי עלמא לא פליגי כי פליגי במחותך
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 4's suggestion that the dispute depends on שמואל
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects tying the dispute to שמואל's rule about נפלים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute could be limited to a fetus born in pieces, with both sides agreeing about a whole נפל

steps.title: Another version: both sages reject שמואל
steps.stepSummary: Another version reads the משנה closely. Because the משנה needs 'most of the body' only when the fetus came out in pieces or feet-first, a fetus that comes out the normal way counts as born from the head. So both sages disagree with שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: the reason most of the body is needed is that it came out in pieces or feet-first. But if it came out the normal way, the head exempts. Both of them do not hold like שמואל, who said the head does not exempt in the case of נפלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way of telling the same discussion. In this version, it learns from the משנה that both sages reject שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only talks about unusual births: in pieces or feet-first. So a normal, head-first birth must count as birth from the head, even for a נפל. Since neither sage argues with the משנה, neither can hold like שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the discussion
Reversed: born feet-first
In its proper way: born head-first and whole
The head exempts: the head coming out counts as birth
Babies who are not able to live

phrases.english: Another version:
The reason most of the body is needed is that it came out in pieces or feet-first,
but if it came out the normal way, the head exempts.
Both of them do not hold like שמואל,
for שמואל said:
The head does not exempt in the case of נפלים.

steps.triggerLanguage: לישנא אחרינא טעמא דיצא מחותך או מסורס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the discussion in Steps 4-5, concluding that both sages reject שמואל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the משנה's wording, a normal head-first birth counts from the head, so both רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן reject שמואל's rule

steps.title: A third version: the sages argue directly about שמואל
steps.stepSummary: Some teach the dispute on its own, not attached to the משנה. רבי אלעזר says the head is not like most of the body. רבי יוחנן says it is. They argue about שמואל's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are those who teach this teaching on its own. רבי אלעזר said: the head is not like most of the limbs. רבי יוחנן said: the head is like most of the limbs. And they argue about שמואל's rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third version. Here the two sages argue openly about whether the head counts for a נפל, which is exactly שמואל's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the dispute is not about a fetus in pieces at all. רבי אלעזר agrees with שמואל that a נפל's head does not count as birth. רבי יוחנן disagrees.

keyTerms.meaning: On its own: as a separate teaching, not attached to the משנה
Most of the limbs: most of the body
They argue about

phrases.english: There are those who teach
this teaching on its own,
רבי אלעזר said:
The head is not like most of the limbs,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: הָרֹאשׁ כְּרוֹב אֵבָרִים,
phrases.english: and רבי יוחנן said: The head is like most of the limbs,
and they argue about שמואל's rule.
phrases.notes: רבי אלעזר follows שמואל, and רבי יוחנן does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: איכא דמתני לה להא שמעתתא באפי נפשה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third version that matches the suggestion in Step 4, taught as an independent dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר: a נפל's head does not count as most of the body, like שמואל. רבי יוחנן: it does.

steps.title: The משנה's wording challenges רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists 'in pieces' and 'feet-first' as two different cases. So 'in pieces' must mean the head came out first. Yet the משנה still requires most of the body, which is hard for רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: if it came out in pieces or feet-first, once most of it comes out, it counts as born. Since the משנה says 'feet-first' separately, the 'in pieces' case must be one where it came out head-first. And still the משנה says it counts as born only when most of it comes out. This is difficult for רבי יוחנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's position by reading the wording of the משנה carefully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'in pieces' already included feet-first births, the משנה would not need to mention 'feet-first' separately. So the 'in pieces' case must be a head-first birth. Even then, the משנה requires most of the body, which contradicts רבי יוחנן's view that the head alone counts.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication: we can learn from this that
Like one who was born
A difficulty: a strong challenge

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'in pieces' and 'feet-first' describe the same case. The challenge only works because the משנה lists them as two separate cases.

phrases.english: We learned: if it came out in pieces or feet-first,
once most of it comes out, it counts as born.
Since the משנה says 'feet-first' as its own case,
we learn that the 'in pieces' case came out the normal way,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָאָמַר מִשֶּׁיֵּצֵא רוּבּוֹ הֲרֵי זֶה כְּיָלוּד —
phrases.english: and still it says that only once most of it comes out does it count as born,
this is difficult for רבי יוחנן!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה to challenge רבי יוחנן's position
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that if the head came out, the head alone counts as birth, even for a fetus born in pieces
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Because the משנה lists 'feet-first' separately, its 'in pieces' case must be head-first. Yet it still requires most of the body, which contradicts רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: The משנה Means In Pieces And Feet-First Together
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the משנה speaks of a fetus that came out in pieces and also feet-first, so the head never came out first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן can say to you: read the משנה as 'it came out in pieces AND feet-first.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן defends himself against the difficulty from Step 8. He says the משנה's case is a fetus that came out both in pieces and feet-first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difficulty was that 'in pieces' seemed to mean the head came out first, yet the משנה still required most of the body. רבי יוחנן says the משנה's case is feet-first, so the head did not come out first. That is why most of the body is needed, and his rule that the head counts is not contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: Cut into pieces; the fetus came out in parts
Reversed; the fetus came out feet-first
'Say' or 'read it as'; introduces a new way of reading a text

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan can say to you:
Read it as: it came out in pieces and feet-first.
phrases.notes: He is reading the משנה's 'or' as if it said 'and', so the two describe one case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised against רבי יוחנן in Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה so that the two descriptions are one combined case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'In pieces' and 'feet-first' are separate cases, so 'in pieces' means head-first, and the משנה still needs most of the body.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's case is feet-first as well as in pieces, so the head never came out first.

steps.title: But The משנה Says 'Or'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the משנה uses the word 'or', which separates the two cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה says 'or'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יוחנן's answer. The word 'or' in the משנה shows two separate cases, not one combined case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's answer turned 'in pieces OR feet-first' into 'in pieces AND feet-first.' The גמרא says the wording does not allow that, because 'or' means either one alone is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Or'; separates two different cases
'But look'; opens a challenge from the text itself

phrases.english: But it teaches 'or'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rereading offered in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reading of the משנה as 'in pieces and feet-first'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'or' in the משנה shows two independent cases, so they cannot be merged into one case.

steps.title: In Pieces Or Whole, But Both Feet-First
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the 'or' differently. It means in pieces or whole, and in both cases the fetus came out feet-first.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: it came out in pieces or whole, and in both cases feet-first. Once most of it comes out, it counts as born.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps the word 'or' but explains what it is choosing between. The choice is pieces versus whole, and both cases are feet-first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the 'or' fits the wording, and רבי יוחנן's point still holds. Every case in the משנה is feet-first, so needing most of the body says nothing about a fetus whose head came out first. The head can still count as birth in that case, even if the fetus is in pieces.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what it means'; explains the true meaning of a text
Whole; in one piece
Most of it; the majority of the body
Like one who is born; it has the status of a birth

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
it came out in pieces or whole,
and both this and that came out feet-first —
once most of it comes out, it is like one who is born.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: יָצָא מְחוּתָּךְ אוֹ שָׁלֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'or' objection of Step 10 and saves רבי יוחנן's reading.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'or' is between 'in pieces' and 'whole,' and both are feet-first. So רבי יוחנן's rule that the head counts still stands.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, the משנה's rule of 'most of the body' is only about a fetus that came out feet-first. When the head comes out first, the head counts as birth.

steps.title: רב פפא Links The Dispute To A ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the dispute between רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר matches a dispute in a ברייתא. There the תנא קמא requires most of the body, and רבי יוסי says 'when it comes out the proper way.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: this is like a dispute between תנאים. If it came out in pieces or feet-first, once most of it comes out it counts as born. רבי יוסי says: once it comes out the proper way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings a ברייתא to show that the dispute between the אמוראים already appears among the תנאים. This step sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא says the two אמוראים are repeating an older argument. But רבי יוסי's short words, 'when it comes out the proper way,' are unclear. So the גמרא will need to explain them before the comparison makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Like the תנאים'; this dispute matches an earlier dispute between תנאים
In its proper way; head-first, as a normal birth

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: it is like a dispute between תנאים,
if it came out in pieces or feet-first —
once most of it comes out, it is like one who is born.
Rabbi Yosei says: once it comes out in its proper way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the defense of רבי יוחנן ends, רב פפא connects the dispute between רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן on the משנה (Steps 2-3) to a dispute between תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute between רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר matches the dispute between the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי in a ברייתא.

steps.title: What Does רבי יוסי Mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יוסי means by 'when it comes out the proper way.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what רבי יוסי's words mean. This question prepares for רב פפא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, רבי יוסי seems to say that a feet-first fetus never counts as born, even after most of it comes out. That is hard to accept. So the גמרא needs a clear explanation of what he is adding to the תנא קמא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is he saying?'; asks for the meaning of an unclear statement

phrases.english: What is he saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of רבי יוסי's statement in the ברייתא quoted in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי יוסי means by 'when it comes out the proper way,' and how he differs from the תנא קמא.

steps.title: The תנא קמא Says The Head Counts, רבי יוסי Needs Most Of The Body
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains the ברייתא. The תנא קמא says that when the fetus comes out the normal way, the head counts as birth. רבי יוסי says that even then, most of the body must come out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said, this is what it means: if it came out in pieces and feet-first, once most of it comes out it counts as born. But if it came out the proper way, the head already counts. רבי יוסי says: it counts once most of it comes out, and only when it comes out the proper way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains both opinions in the ברייתא. This shows how they match רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא needs most of the body only for a feet-first fetus. From his words we learn that head-first, the head alone counts as birth, even in pieces. That is רבי יוחנן's view. רבי יוסי requires both most of the body and a proper, head-first way of coming out, so the head alone is not enough. That is רבי אלעזר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But this'; introduces what we learn from the words that were said
The head 'exempts'; once the head comes out, the fetus counts as born, with the full legal effect of a birth

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבי יוסי's 'proper way' as making things easier. In רב פפא's reading it adds a condition, so you need both most of the body and a head-first exit. The head alone is never enough for him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר are not inventing a new argument. Each one follows a different תנא in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said, this is what it is saying:
if it came out in pieces or feet-first —
once most of it comes out, it is like one who is born,
but if it came out the proper way, the head already exempts.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: מִשֶּׁיֵּצֵא רוּבּוֹ כְּתִקְנוֹ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: once most of it comes out, in its proper way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13 by explaining both opinions in the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא says the head counts as birth when the fetus comes out the proper way, even in pieces. רבי יוסי needs most of the body plus a proper way. So the תנא קמא matches רבי יוחנן, and רבי יוסי matches רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא and רבי יוחנן say that head-first, the head counts as birth. רבי יוסי and רבי אלעזר say that for a fetus in pieces, the head is not enough, and most of the body must come out the proper way.

steps.title: רב זביד objects: feet-first, most of the body must count
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד points out that רב פפא's reading leads to a strange result. For a feet-first baby, even most of the body would not count as birth. But we hold רובו ככולו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד objects: Your reading implies that in a feet-first birth, even when most of the body comes out, it does not exempt. But we hold that most of something is like all of it!
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד attacks the explanation רב פפא just gave in Step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב פפא's reading, רבי יוסי needs two things: the baby comes out the proper way, and most of the body comes out. That would mean a feet-first baby never counts, even when most of it has come out. That cannot be right, because רובו ככולו means 'most of it' should be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it; a strong challenge to someone's statement
By implication; it follows from what you said
Reversed; the baby came out feet-first
Exempts; here, counts as the birth, so the next baby is not the בכור
Most of something is treated like all of it

phrases.english: Rav Zevid objects to it:
This implies that in a reversed (feet-first) case,
even most of it does not exempt?
But we hold that most of it is like all of it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's reading of the ברייתא from Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's reading of רבי יוסי as requiring both the proper way and most of the body
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading means a feet-first baby would not count even when most of it has come out. This goes against the accepted rule רובו ככולו.

steps.title: רב זביד's new reading of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד rereads the ברייתא. A baby born in pieces and feet-first counts once most of it is out. If it was born head-first, the head is enough, even in pieces. רבי יוסי says the head counts only when the baby comes out the proper way, alive and whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב זביד says this is what the ברייתא means: If the baby came out in pieces and feet-first, it counts as born once most of it comes out. But if it came out the proper way, the head exempts. רבי יוסי says: Only when it comes out the proper way, alive.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד drops רב פפא's reading and gives his own explanation of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the 'most of it' rule applies to the feet-first case, so רובו ככולו is kept. The disagreement moves to a head-first baby born in pieces. The תנא קמא says the head is enough even then. רבי יוסי says the head counts only for a baby born whole and alive. If it comes out in pieces, most of the body is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means; rereading a source
Cut into pieces
Like a born child
In its proper way; head-first
Alive; here, the way a living, whole baby is born

steps.confusionAlert: In רב זביד's reading, 'in pieces and feet-first' is one case, so 'most of it' is needed. The real argument is about a baby that came out head-first but in pieces.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Zevid said,
this is what it is saying:
If it came out in pieces and reversed,
once most of it comes out, it is like a born child;
but if in its proper way, the head exempts.
phrases.notes: He means even if it came out in pieces, as long as it came head-first.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Once it comes out in its proper way, alive.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב זְבִיד, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב זביד's own objection by rereading the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי needs both the proper way and most of the body, so a feet-first baby never counts
steps.terutzMaskana: A feet-first baby counts once most of it is out. The argument is only about a head-first baby born in pieces.

steps.title: A ברייתא that says exactly what רב זביד said
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the same wording as רב זביד's reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: If the baby came out in pieces and feet-first, it counts as born once most of it comes out. But if it came out the proper way, the head exempts. רבי יוסי says: Only when it comes out the proper way, alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רב זביד with a ברייתא that spells out his reading word for word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב זביד's explanation is no longer just a guess. An actual ברייתא says the same thing. This confirms that the feet-first case needs most of the body, and that רבי יוסי's point is about a whole, living baby.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way; a ברייתא that supports what was just said

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
If it came out in pieces (or) reversed,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the 'or' in round brackets, so it reads 'in pieces and reversed,' matching רב זביד.

phrases.english: once most of it comes out, it is like a born child;
but if in its proper way, the head exempts.
Rabbi Yosei says:
Once it comes out in its proper way, alive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב זביד's reading from Step 16
steps.raayaObject: רב זביד's reading of the ברייתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same wording

steps.title: 'The proper way' means most of the head came out
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. It explains that a baby born the proper way counts once most of its head has come out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is 'the proper way, alive'? Once most of its head comes out.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a quick question about its own words and answers it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we only knew that 'the head exempts' when the baby comes out the proper way. Here the ברייתא adds a detail: the whole head does not need to come out. Most of the head is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Which is it? What exactly counts?
Most of its head

phrases.english: And what is 'its proper way, alive'?
Once most of its head comes out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא from Step 17 continues and defines its own term
steps.sheelahInformationSought: At what point does a baby born the proper way count as born?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Once most of its head has come out

steps.title: Three opinions on what counts as 'most of the head'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what counts as 'most of the head.' רבי יוסי says the temples. אבא חנן in the name of רבי יהושע says the forehead. יש אומרים say the bulges at the back of the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is 'most of its head'? רבי יוסי says: Once its temples come out. אבא חנן in the name of רבי יהושע says: Once its forehead comes out. And some say: Once the bulges at the back of its head can be seen.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks how to measure 'most of the head' and gives three different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each opinion picks a different body landmark to mark 'most of the head': the temples, the forehead, or the bulges of the head above the neck. The question is not whether most of the head is needed, only where exactly that point is.

keyTerms.meaning: Its temples, the sides of the head
Its forehead
The 'corners' of its head, the bulge at the back of the head above the neck
Some say; an unnamed opinion

steps.whatToRemember: In רב זביד's reading, a baby born in pieces and feet-first counts once most of the body is out (רובו ככולו). For a head-first baby, the תנא קמא says the head counts as birth. רבי יוסי says the head counts only for a whole, living baby, and then most of the head is enough. There are three opinions on how to measure 'most of the head': the temples, the forehead, or the corners of the head above the neck.

phrases.english: And what is 'most of its head'?
Rabbi Yosei says: Once its temples come out.

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּא חָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Abba Chanan says in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua:
Once its forehead comes out.
phrases.notes: Both bracketed words mean 'comes out.' The square-bracket one fits better, since פדחת is a feminine word.

phrases.english: And some say: Once the corners of its head are seen.
phrases.notes: The 'corners' are the bulge of the head right above the neck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term 'most of its head' from Step 18
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly counts as 'most of the head'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three opinions: the temples, the forehead, or the corners of the head

steps.title: The משנה: a miscarriage of unknown kind
steps.stepSummary: A woman who miscarries something unidentified keeps the rules for both a boy and a girl. If it might not have been a baby at all, she also keeps the rules of נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a woman miscarries and we don't know what it was, she keeps the rules for a boy and for a girl. If we don't know whether it was a baby at all, she keeps the rules for a boy, for a girl, and for נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic: what a woman does after a miscarriage when we don't know what came out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After a girl, a woman is impure for 14 days; after a boy, her 'pure blood' days end at 40, not 80. So when we don't know, she takes the stricter side of each: 14 days impure and only 40 days of pure blood. If maybe it was not a baby at all, she may have no pure-blood days, so any blood she sees is treated as נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: a woman who miscarries
literally 'she sits'; here, she keeps the rules (of a certain status)
a baby or fetus that counts as a real birth
a woman made impure by her regular period

steps.confusionAlert: 'Sits for a male and for a female' does not mean she keeps two separate periods one after the other. It means she follows whichever rule is stricter at each point.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: A woman who miscarries and it is not known what it is
she keeps the rules for a male and for a female.
phrases.notes: In practice: 14 days impure like after a girl, but only 40 days of pure blood like after a boy.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין יָדוּעַ אִם וָלָד הָיָה אִם לָאו
phrases.english: If it is not known whether it was a baby or not
she keeps the rules for a male, for a female, and for נדה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic, separate from the earlier discussion of what counts as birth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the miscarriage cannot be identified, she keeps the stricter rules of both boy and girl. If it may not have been a baby at all, she also keeps the rules of נדה.

steps.title: Miscarriage in a river: follow the majority
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that a woman who miscarried into a river brings the birth קרבן, and it is eaten, because most women give birth to a real baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: If a woman crossed a river and miscarried, she brings a קרבן and it is eaten. We follow the majority of women, and most women give birth to a real baby.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling of רבי יהושע בן לוי. We can't see what fell into the river, but we still treat it as a real baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fetus is lost in the river, so we can't check whether it was fully formed. He relies on רוב: most pregnancies produce a real baby. He is so sure of this that the bird sin-offering may even be eaten. Had she not really owed it, that bird would be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: the offering a woman brings after giving birth
and it is eaten, meaning it is treated as a fully valid offering
majority; we decide an unknown case by what usually happens
a proper, fully formed baby

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how far רוב can go: it is strong enough to allow eating an offering even when the facts are unknown.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ' אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
If she crossed a river and miscarried
she brings an offering, and it is eaten.
Follow the majority of women,
and most women give birth to a proper baby.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי עָבְרָה נָהָר וְהִפִּילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ruling of an אמורא about an unknown miscarriage. It relies on רוב, which seems to clash with the משנה's strictness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who miscarried something unseen brings the birth קרבן, and it is eaten, based on the majority of women.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה's rule of נדה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if we follow the majority, why does the משנה make her keep the rules of נדה? We should assume it was a real baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: If it is not known whether it was a baby, she keeps the rules for a boy, for a girl, and for נדה. Why should she keep the rules of נדה? Let us say: follow the majority of women, and most women give birth to a real baby!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע בן לוי from the last line of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה worries that maybe it was not a baby, so her blood might be נדה blood. By רבי יהושע בן לוי's logic, the majority should tell us it was a real baby. Then she should get the normal pure-blood days after birth, with no worry of נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: why?
let us say; used to suggest what should follow
'pure blood': blood seen in the days after birth that does not make her impure

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: אֵין יָדוּעַ אִם וָלָד הָיָה
phrases.english: We learned: If it is not known whether it was a baby,
she keeps the rules for a male, for a female, and for נדה.
Why should she keep the rules of נדה?
Let us say: follow the majority of women,
and most women give birth to a proper baby!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: אֵין יָדוּעַ אִם וָלָד הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה from step 20 to attack the ruling in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's use of the majority to treat an unknown miscarriage as a real baby.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה does not rely on the majority. It treats the case as possibly not a baby, which goes against his principle.

steps.title: Known to be pregnant vs. not known
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is about a woman not known to be pregnant. רבי יהושע בן לוי is talking about a woman who was known to be pregnant.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is talking about a woman who was not known to be pregnant. When רבי יהושע בן לוי gives his ruling, it is about a woman who was known to be pregnant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by placing the two rulings in two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The majority rule is about pregnant women: most pregnancies end in a real baby. That only helps when we know she was pregnant. In the משנה we never knew she was pregnant, so there is no majority to rely on, and she must worry it was not a baby.

keyTerms.meaning: she was established, known for sure, to be in a certain state
pregnant
an established status that we rely on

steps.whatToRemember: רוב (most women give birth to a real baby) applies only to a woman known to be pregnant. If she was not known to be pregnant, the משנה's strict ruling applies, including נדה.

phrases.english: Our Mishnah is where she was not known to be pregnant,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
phrases.english: and when Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says his ruling,
it is where she was known to be pregnant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22 by splitting the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source is about a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and רבי יהושע בן לוי seemed to be about the same case, so they seemed to clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a woman not known to be pregnant, where there is no majority to rely on. רבי יהושע בן לוי is about a woman known to be pregnant, where the majority applies.

steps.title: An animal left pregnant and came back empty
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that if an animal went out pregnant and came back empty, its next offspring is a doubtful בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: an animal went out full (pregnant) and came back empty. The next one born after it is a בכור out of doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא as a new source to test the rule of רבי יהושע בן לוי. This step only sets up the ruling; the challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the first offspring from the womb is a בכור. If the animal lost a real baby out in the field, the next baby is not a בכור. If what came out was not a real baby, the next one is a real בכור. Since we don't know which happened, the ברייתא calls the next baby a doubtful בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn animal, the first to come out of its mother's womb
Out of doubt; we are not sure of its status
Full, meaning pregnant
Empty, meaning no longer pregnant

phrases.english: Come and hear:
An animal that went out full,
phrases.notes: "Full" means pregnant. It went out to the field to graze.

phrases.english: and came back empty,
the one that comes after it is a firstborn out of doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source about animals to test רבי יהושע בן לוי's majority rule from step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal that left pregnant and returned empty: its next offspring is a doubtful בכור.

steps.title: Why not follow the majority of animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: most animals give birth to a real baby, so the next one should surely not be a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? Follow the majority of animals. Most animals give birth to a real baby, so this next one is an ordinary animal and not a בכור!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא using the majority logic of רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי said we assume a real birth because most pregnancies end that way. Applied here, the animal surely lost a real baby in the field. Then the next baby should be definitely not a בכור, not just a doubtful one.

keyTerms.meaning: Majority; we follow what usually happens
A proper, real offspring
Ordinary, meaning not a בכור

phrases.english: But why?
Follow the majority of animals,
and most animals give birth to a proper offspring,
and this one is ordinary!
phrases.notes: "Ordinary" means it is not a firstborn, because a real baby already came out before it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא of step 24 to attack the majority rule of step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule that we follow the majority of births
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the majority decides, the ברייתא should say the next offspring is definitely not a בכור, not a doubtful one.

steps.title: רבינא: the missing discharge weakens the majority
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that the majority is not strong here, and since the animal showed no discharge before leaving, the majority is weakened.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: we can say that most animals give birth to something that exempts from בכור status, and a few give birth to something that does not. Also, all animals about to give birth have a murky discharge. Since this one did not, the majority is weakened.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא defends the ברייתא by showing why the majority does not decide this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He gives two factors. First, the majority is not complete; some animals give birth to something that does not cancel בכור status. Second, this animal did not show the usual discharge before it went out. That missing sign weakens the majority, so we are left with a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempts from בכור status, so the next baby is not a בכור
Minority
Have a murky discharge, a sign that birth is coming
The majority has been weakened

phrases.english: Ravina said: Because one can say:
most animals give birth to
something that exempts from firstborn status,
and a minority of them give birth to
something that does not exempt from firstborn status,
and all those giving birth have a murky discharge,
and this one, since it did not discharge,
the majority is weakened for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weakening the majority with a missing sign
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The majority of real births should decide that the next offspring is not a בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The animal did not show the usual discharge, so the majority is weakened, and the next offspring stays a doubtful בכור.

steps.title: If ALL animals discharge, this would be a sure בכור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if every birth comes with discharge, then no discharge means no real birth, so the next one is a definite בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If all animals giving birth have a discharge, then since this one did not, it gave birth to nothing real. The next one is a full בכור!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the exact wording of רבינא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא said ALL animals discharge before a birth. If that were true, the missing discharge would prove there was no real birth. Then the ברייתא should say the next one is a definite בכור, not a doubtful one.

keyTerms.meaning: If so ... then; the setup of a logical challenge
A full, definite בכור

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not rejecting רבינא's whole idea. It only shows that the word "all" goes too far, because it would turn a doubt into a certainty.

phrases.english: If all those giving birth have a discharge,
then from the fact that this one did not discharge,
it is a proper firstborn!
phrases.notes: He means the next baby, the one born after this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the word "all" in רבינא's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that all animals discharge before giving birth
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it is always true, the missing discharge proves there was no real birth, so the next baby would be a definite בכור, against the ברייתא.

steps.title: Correct the wording: MOST animals discharge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords רבינא: most animals discharge before birth, so a missing discharge only weakens the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: most animals giving birth have a discharge. Since this one did not, the majority is weakened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of רבינא's answer so that it fits the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing "all" to "most" means the missing discharge is only a weak sign. It does not prove there was no birth. It just weakens the majority of real births, so we have a true doubt, just as the ברייתא says.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say; a correction of the wording
Most animals that give birth

steps.whatToRemember: An animal that left pregnant and came back empty: its next offspring is a doubtful בכור. The majority of real births is weakened because MOST births come with a discharge, and this animal had none.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a majority can be weakened by a missing sign that usually comes with it. It also explains why רבי יהושע בן לוי's majority rule does not decide every case.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
most of those giving birth have a discharge,
and this one, since it did not discharge,
the majority is weakened for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27 by rewording רבינא's answer from "all" to "most".
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All animals discharge, which would make the next baby a definite בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: Most animals discharge, so the missing discharge only weakens the majority, leaving a doubtful בכור.

steps.title: רבין reports a puzzling objection from the case of a forgetful woman
steps.stepSummary: רבין brings a report from ארץ ישראל: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא raised an objection from the case of a טועה, but רבין does not know what the objection is.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came from ארץ ישראל, he said: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא raises an objection from the case of a woman who lost track of her days, but I do not know what the objection is.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין reports that an objection was raised from the law of a טועה. He openly admits that he does not understand how that law makes a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a report of a challenge, not a full challenge yet. We are told where the attack comes from (the law of a טועה), but not how it works. The target is an earlier ruling, which the context links to רבי יהושע בן לוי. Because רבין himself does not understand it, the גמרא will have to work out the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who has lost track of her cycle and does not know which days are which
An objection or refutation
When he came, used for a sage who brought teachings from ארץ ישראל to בבל

steps.confusionAlert: רבין is not making the objection himself, and he is not agreeing with it. He is only passing on a report, and he admits he does not understand it.

phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: מֵתִיב רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא טוֹעָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina raises an objection from a forgetful woman,
but I do not know what the objection is.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַבִּין אָמַר: מֵתִיב רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא טוֹעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the animal-בכור discussion and opens a new challenge, reported by רבין.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling (Step 21) that a miscarriage is treated as a real birth because most women give birth to a proper baby.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only the source of the challenge, the law of a טועה, is named here. How it attacks the ruling is worked out on the next amud.

steps.title: What is the law of the forgetful woman?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law of the טועה is, and introduces a ברייתא that will explain it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it? As it is taught in a ברייתא:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what this law of a טועה actually says. It is setting up the next move by introducing a ברייתא that will lay out the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We cannot understand the objection until we know the source it comes from. So the גמרא first asks for the text of the law itself. The word דתניא tells us the answer is a ברייתא, which will be quoted next.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? A request to identify a source that was only mentioned briefly
A teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself

phrases.english: What is it? As it is taught in a baraita:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the objection named in step 29, so the objection can be worked out.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly the law of a טועה says.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא is introduced as the answer. Its text is quoted on the next amud.
